texts.preamble: Food Safety Officer vs Pradeep Kumar And Ors on 11 July, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Pranav Joshi, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, New Delhi, Patiala House Courts, Delhi Cr. Cases No. 924/2021 Cnr No. Dlnd02-002606-2021 Fso Vs. Pradeep Kumar & Ors. U/S 3/26/27/59 Fss Act, 2006 1) The date of commission : 14.02.2020 of offence 2) The name of the complainant : Fso Kuldeep Singh Suman 3) The name & parentage of accused : 1. Sh. Praveen Kumar, C/o M/s Symphony Banquets, Unit of Multiple Hospitality, D-11, Udyog Nagar, Rohtak Road, Delhi. R / o C-44/149 , Street No. 10, Gamri Extn., North East Delhi . 2. M/s Multiple Hospitality, D-11, Udyog Nagar, Rohtak Road, Delhi. 3. Sh. Sarvagya Sujan, Ct. Case No. 924/2021 Fso Vs. Pradeep Kumar & Ors. Page No.1/10 S/o Late Sh. Ram Niwas, M/s S. S. Paneer World,
texts.facts: This is a complaint instituted under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'FSS Act') for violation of section 3/26/27 punishable under section 59 of FSS Act. 2. Brief facts leading to filing of the present complaint are that on 14.02.2020 at about 02.30 pm, Sh. Kuldeep Singh Suman, Food Safety Officer (FSO) along with Sh. Naubat Singh visited the premises of M/s Symphony Banquets - A Unit of Multiple Hospitality and disclosed his identity to the Food Business Operator (FBO) Sh. Pradeep Kumar, who was conducting the business of the food articles including 'Paneer'. After inspection of the premises, complainant showed his intention of purchasing a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis, where the said food article was stored in an open tray bearing no label declaration for ready for use for the preparation of Paneer Tikka, Shahi Paneer & other dishes of Paneer which were intended for human consumption, to which he agreed. The complainant tried to associate some public witnesses by requesting passersby but when none came forward, then complainant requested to Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant, for witnessing the proceedings to which he agreed and joined as witness in the sample proceedings. Thereafter, the complainant purchased a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis from FBO Sh. Pradeep Kumar and price of the sample was disclosed by the FBO to be Rs. 236/- which was offered to the FBO in cash but the same was not accepted by him as sample was not for direct sale. 3. Thereafter, the sample consisted of approx. 1 kg of 'Paneer' taken after cutting it into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean and dry knife provided by FBO in a clean and dry tray. The same was mixed properly with the help of clean and dry steel spoon provided by FBO by rotating it Food Safety Officer vs Pradeep Kumar And Ors on 11 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174035877/ 2 in all possible directions several times. The sample of aforesaid food article divided in to four counterparts then and there by putting it equally in four clean and dry glass bottles with the help of same spoon. Thereafter, 20 drops of formalin added in each counter part of sample with the help of a clean and dry dropper. Each glass bottle containing the sample was separately marked, packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of the Food Safety and standard Act, 2006 and Rules & Regulations made thereunder. The signature of the FBO were obtained on the Designated Officer's slip bearing signature of the then Designated Officer Sh. Bal Mukund and also on the wrapper of the bottles containing the sample, in such a manner that the same was partly visible on the then Designated Officer slip and partly on the wrapper of the sample bottles. The complainant also obtained signatures of the FBO on the labels of all counter parts of the sample. Notice in Form VA was prepared at the spot and copy of the same was given to FBO. A copy of this notice was also served to supplier, M/s S. S. Paneer World. The Food Business Operator did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. The Panchnama and Raid report was also prepared at the spot. All the sampled documents prepared by the complainant were read over and explained to FBO in Hindi, who signed the same after understanding the same. These documents were also signed by the complainant himself and by the witness Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant. 4. Thereafter, one counter part of the aforesaid sample of 'Paneer' bearing sample No. 747/1051/22/2020 and the then Designated Officer Code No. 07/DO-26/15250 was sent to the Food Analyst, Govt. of NCT of Delhi for analysis on 17.02.2020. The FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. The remaining two counterparts of the sample along with two forms VI in a sealed packet as well as the fourth counterpart of the sample along with one form VI in a separate sealed packet were deposited to the then Designated Officer Sh. Bal Mukund on 17.02.2020. The Food Analyst in his report No. FSS/290/2020 dated 20.02.2020 has opined, "The sample is substandard because moisture exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 60.0%." The then Designated Officer of District West, Sh. Bal Mukund sent a copy of the intimation letter along with analysis report of Food Analyst to the FBO on 21.02.2020 for giving them an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under section 46(4) of the FSS Act, 2006 for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory. The FBO preferred an appeal against the report of Food Analyst under rule 2.4.6 (1) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 before the Designated Officer of District West Sh. R. K. Bhaskar on 12.03.2020 and one counterpart of sample was sent to the Director, Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad (U.P.) on 13.03.2020. 5. The Director, Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad vide certificate No. 191/Apr/20-ND dated 16.04.2020 has opined, "The sample of Paneer does not conform to the standards laid down under Regulation no. 2.1.16 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive) Regulation, 2011, as the sample shows the presence of B.R. Reading above the maximum prescribed limit, indicating the presence of foreign fat. The sample is thus unsafe under Section 3(1)(zz) (iv) of FSS Act, 2006." Thereafter, a letter dated 03.06.2020 sent by the Designated Officer of Dist. West Sh. R. K. Bhaskar to the Director, Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad regarding errors in certificate of Analysis No. 191/Apr/20-ND dated 16.04.2020 and a corrigendum dated 16.06.2020 was received from Referral Food Laboratory, as per which "code no. 07/DO-26/15250 & Sample no. Food Safety Officer vs Pradeep Kumar And Ors on 11 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174035877/ 3 747/1051/22/2020" on first line of page No. 1 of 2 of the COA be read in lieu of Code No. 07/DO-25/2020 and sample No. 747/1031/22/2020, as given on sample label, and in the third line of opinion part of second page 2 of 2 of COA for the sample of Paneer to be read as "B.R. Reading below the minimum prescribed limit." in lieu of "B.R. Reading above the maximum prescribed limit." 6. It is further averred that M/s Symphony Banquets- A Unit of Multiple Hospitalityis a partnership firm having two partners namely, Sh. Suhel Nagpal and Sh. Jagdish Lal Nagpal. However, said firm has appointed Sh. Pradeep Kumar as nominee under FSS Rules, 2011 and at the time of sampling, he was looking after the day to day conduct of its business, therefore, he was responsible for conducting day to day business and as such in-charge of and liable for offence. It is further alleged that M/s Multiple Hospitality being a partnership firm was also liable for offence. It is further alleged that the above said food article 'Paneer' was manufactured by M/s S. S. Paneer World and supplied to M/s Symphony Banquets. It is also alleged that M/s S. S. Paneer World is a proprietorship firm and Sh. Sarvagya Sujan is the proprietor of said firm and looks after the day to day business of the firm and as such he is in-charge of and responsible for the conduct of its business and liable for the offence. It is further alleged that the above mentioned accused violated the provisions of Section 26(1) and 26(2) (i) read with Sections 3(1)(zz)(iv) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 & also violated Regulation No. 2.1.16 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011. Further, Sh. Sarvagya Sujan, proprietor of M/s S.S. Paneer World has also violated the provision of Sections 27(1) & 27(2)(c), which is punishable under Section 59 (i) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. After conclusion of the investigation, the case containing the statutory documents and Food Analyst report, was sent by Sh. R. K. Bhaskar, Designated Officer, District West to the Commissioner (Food Safety), Department of Food Safety, Government of NCT of Delhi, who accorded the consent under Section 42(4) of the FSS Act, 2006 for the prosecution of accused in exercise of the power vested in him under section 30(2)(e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and directed the complainant to institute the prosecution. 7. Upon filing of the present complaint, cognizance was taken vide order dated 11.02.2021. Upon service of summons, appearance was entered by accused No.1 who also represented accused No.2. However, accused No.3 was not served with the summons as he had already expired and vide order dated 26.03.2022, proceedings against the accused No.3 stood abated. After complying with the provision under section 207 Cr.P.C, vide order dated 02.07.2022, notice for the offences under section 3/26/27/59 of FSS Act was served upon the accused No.1 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the case was fixed for prosecution evidence. 8. The prosecution examined FSO Sh. Kuldeep Singh as PW1. He deposed on the lines of the complaint and relied upon the following documents: (a) FBO receipt Ex. PW1/A, (b) Form VA Ex. PW1/B, Food Safety Officer vs Pradeep Kumar And Ors on 11 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174035877/ 4 (d) Raid Report Ex. PW1/D, (e) Aadhar card and FSSAI licence of FBO Mark 1/1 and Mark 1/2, (f) Receipt of sample to DO Ex. PW1/E, The accused admitted the witnesses at serial No. 2 to 6 and thus, the remaining witnesses were not examined. Accordingly, the prosecution evidence was closed on 12.02.2025. Thereafter, statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded in which the accused No.1 stated that he was innocent as the food article was supplied by accused No.3. 10.
texts.arguments: It was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in P. Unnikrishnan Vs. Food Inspector, Palghat Municipality, Kerala, 1996 2 PFAC 25, that the supplier was entitled to benefit of warranty u/s 19(2) of PFA for a food article manufactured and supplied by the manufacturer firm. Reliance is placed on the judgment of Prakash Chand Vs. State of M. P., 1993 I PFAC 28. 13.
